properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 21 at 10:14PM PDT until October 22 at 2:00AM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
FFWLOX

The National Weather Service in Los Angeles/Oxnard has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southeastern Santa Barbara County in southwestern California...

* Until 200 AM PDT.

* At 1014 PM PDT, gauge reports indicated thunderstorms producing
increasingly heavy rain across the warned area. The expected
rainfall rate is 1 to 1.5 inches in 1 hour. Dangerous flash
flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly, dangerous rock
slides and mud slides are also expected.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding. Dangerous rock slides and mud slides.

SOURCE...Gauges reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Santa Barbara, Montecito, Carpinteria and Summerland.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued October 21 at 10:07PM PDT until October 21 at 10:45PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
For the following areas...
East Santa Barbara Channel from Pt. Conception to Pt. Mugu CA
including Santa Cruz Island...
Inner waters from Point Mugu to San Mateo Pt. CA including Santa
Catalina and Anacapa Islands...
Outer waters from Santa Cruz Island to San Clemente Island to 60 NM
offshore including San Nicolas and Santa Barbara Islands...
Waters from Pt. Sal to Santa Cruz Island CA and westward 60 nm
including San Miguel and Santa Rosa Islands...

At 1007 PM PDT, severe thunderstorms capable of producing waterspouts
were located along a line extending from 30 nm northeast of Point
Conception to 9 nm south of Goleta Point to 13 nm northeast of San
Nicolas Island, moving northeast at 15 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts to nearly 50 knots.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

Locations impacted include...
West Point Santa Cruz Island, Ventura Harbor, San Nicolas Island,
Anacapa Island, and Santa Rosa Island.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 21 at 8:27PM MST until October 22 at 2:30AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Coconino County in north central Arizona...

* Until 230 AM MST /330 AM MDT/ Tonight.

* At 827 PM MST /927 PM MDT/, a river gauge on the Little Colorado
River near the Colorado River reported a rapid rise of 5 feet from
thunderstorms earlier today. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to
1 inch are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing
or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...River gauge reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
normally dry washes, urban areas, highways, streets and
underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Little Colorado River Navajo Tribal Park and Salt Trail Canyon.

This includes the following highways...
the Colorado River near mile marker 62. State Route 64 near mile
marker 282...and between mile markers 285 and 286.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Blue Water Base Camp, Old Fish Camp Site and Above LCR Camp Site.

This includes the following swimming holes...
Blue Water Base Camp.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Bekihatso Wash, Colorado River, Little Colorado River, Moenkopi
Wash and Sheep Wash.
properties.instruction:
Flooding of washes and creeks will occur, some dirt roads will become
muddy and impassable. Paved roads and underpasses could become
flooded as well.

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued October 21 at 10:07PM PDT until October 21 at 10:45PM PDT by NWS Las Vegas NV
properties.description:
SVRVEF

The National Weather Service in Las Vegas has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
North Central Mohave County in northwestern Arizona...
Southeastern Lincoln County in south central Nevada...
Northeastern Clark County in southern Nevada...

* Until 1045 PM PDT /1045 PM MST/.

* At 1007 PM PDT /1007 PM MST/, a severe thunderstorm was located
over Mesquite, moving north at 45 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect wind damage to
roofs, siding, and trees.

* Locations impacted include...
Mesquite, Beaver Dam, Littlefield and Bunkerville.

This includes the following highways...
Interstate 15 in Nevada between mile markers 110 and 120. Interstate
15 in Arizona between mile markers 0 and 8.
properties.instruction:
Seek shelter inside a well-built structure and stay away from
windows. This storm is capable of producing damaging winds and large
hail.

properties.areaDesc: Garfield, UT; Kane, UT; San Juan, UT
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 21 at 12:35PM MDT until October 22 at 12:15PM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...San Juan County in southeastern Utah...
Southwestern Garfield County in southern Utah...
Kane County in southern Utah...

* WHEN...Until 1215 PM MDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of normally dry washes, slot canyons, rivers,
creeks, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations is imminent
or occurring. Prolonged and widespread moderate to heavy rainfall
will continue trough at least Thursday morning. This coupled with
near-saturated soils will allow rapidly increasing flows across all
waterways within the warned area, including all of the Glen Canyon
National Recreation Area. Increasingly high flows are expected in,
but not limited to...the Paria River, Wahweep Creek, Warm Creek,
Last Chance Creek, Croton Canyon, and the Escalante River Basin and
tributaries. Many backcountry roads within this area are expected
to become impassable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1208 PM MDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges continue
to indicate heavy rain. Flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the warned area. Between 0.25 and 0.75 inches of rain
have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2.5 inches are possible in
the warned area through Thursday morning.
- Glen Canyon National Recreation Area, including the Escalante
region. Kodachrome State Park, Tropic, Cannonville, Escalante,
and Big Water
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Stay away or be swept away. River banks can become unstable and
unsafe.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 21 at 9:49PM MST until October 22 at 2:00AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Moenkopi Wash in...
Coconino County in north central Arizona...

* Until 200 AM MST /300 AM MDT/.

* At 949 PM MST /1049 PM MDT/, Moenkopi Wash remained above major
flood stage, with only a gradual decrease over the last hour. With
additional heavy rain expected in the Moenkopi Wash basin, flooding
is expected to continue. Flash flooding is already occurring.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Moenkopi Wash.

SOURCE...River gauge reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Moenkopi Wash.

* For Moenkopi Wash near Tuba City:
At 8:45pm MST /9:45pm MDT/ the stage was 33.54 feet.
Flood Stage is 27.0 feet.
Impacts:
At 27.0 feet: At 27.0 feet water begins to encroach on homes in
lower Moenkopi Village and floods crop fields along the river.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Moenkopi.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Hamblin Wash, Begashibito Wash, Little Colorado River, Moenkopi
Wash and Fivemile Wash.
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Stay away or be swept away! The banks of creeks and washes are
unstable and unsafe during any flooding event.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 21 at 9:21PM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.Persistent northeast winds have caused river levels on the St Johns
at Astor to rise into Moderate Flood Stage. The river is forecast to
climb slowly through Moderate Flood Stage through the end of this
week. There is potential for levels to approach Major Flood Stage
next week after northeast winds increase again.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on
or near Wildhog and Bonnet roads become inaccessible with several
inches of water inside homes along the river and canals. Docks at
Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely submerged.
Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with yards
completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads flooded
in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on Juno
Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 PM EDT Wednesday the stage was 3.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 PM EDT Wednesday was 3.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 3.2 feet.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Thursday morning at 1130 AM EDT.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 21 at 9:11PM PDT until October 22 at 2:00AM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
FFWLOX

The National Weather Service in Los Angeles/Oxnard has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southern Santa Barbara County in southwestern California...

* Until 200 AM PDT.

* At 911 PM PDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. The expected rainfall rate is
0.7 to 1 inch in 1 hour. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to
begin shortly. Rock slides and mud slides are likely.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms. Rock slides and
mud slides.

SOURCE...Gauges reported.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas. Rock slides and mud slides.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Portions of southern Santa Barbara County, including the Santa Ynez
Range and the South Coast, and the City of Santa Barbara.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Water can rise rapidly in hilly terrain and in urban areas.

Rock slides and mud slides are likely, especially around mountain and
foothill roadways.
